original version: |corr(SPY, oc)| < 0.5 x corr(SPY, cc) (absolute value)
new version: corr(SPY, oc) < 0.5 x corr(SPY, cc) (signed); both versions kept in sanity.json

original version: pct_change on the combined table of all markets' dates, then select a market's dates
new version: returns computed on each market's own calendar first (local_returns), with a unit test
why: the union calendar put a missing day before every Asian date that followed a US-only date, so those returns became NaN; noticed because the sanity-check pair counts did not match the saved calendar
did the conclusion change: no: correlations moved by at most 0.01

original version: index-level open-to-close check only
new version: added a stock-level check (mean over each market's stocks)
why: ^TWII's 09:00 value is stale (uses previous closes of stocks that have not traded), which inflated its oc correlation (0.21)

what: Follower items: raw vs home-index residual
original version: planned: Asian followers as residuals against their home index
new version: main design: raw follower moves, with the controls doing the work by comparison; residuals against an ex-stock home index as a robustness check
why: TSMC is ~35% of ^TWII and Samsung ~20% of ^KS11: a residual removes much of the signal and gives non-AI controls a mechanical negative response; decided BEFORE running Stage 2
did the conclusion change: no: robustness table gives the same verdict with ex-stock residuals

original version: use ^TOPX (TOPIX) for Japan
new version: ^N225 with the stock taken out

what: Index weights for the ex-stock index
original version: official time-varying weights
new version: approximate constant weights (author estimates, documented in data/README.md)
why: no free source of daily index weights; robustness check only

original version: each group on all of its own valid dates
new version: only US dates with a valid follower date in all three Asian markets (2,269 of 2,676; 407 dropped)
why: so every group is tested on exactly the same days (paired comparisons)

what: Extra secondary group (f) and number of chance copies
original version: groups a-e; 3 time-shifted copies (as in the baseline)
new version: added (f) US non-AI -> Asian AI as a secondary control; 5 copies
why: (f) was named as a criterion in review; more copies only reduce noise in the chance level

original version: 95% percentile interval of the block bootstrap (pre-registration wording)
new version: estimate +/- 1.96 x bootstrap standard error; both shown side by side
why: percentile intervals were biased low (some point estimates outside their own interval): resampling adds noise to each rule's yes/no direction call, pulling real rules toward 50%
did the conclusion change: no: the pre-registered verdict is the same under both methods

original version: known company links only
new version: added sector labels (chip-equipment, memory peer) after seeing that most lasting edges were chipmaker -> chip-equipment
why: most kept edges had no direct supplier link

what: Chance baseline for the SPY reversal rules
original version: real minus time-shifted chance rules, as everywhere else
new version: direction-right share compared with 50% (the mirror check); chance rules reported but not used
why: with only two leader items the shifted copies mine the same rules, scored on the same real days, so the chance rules inherit the real reversal (80% real vs 79% chance)
did the conclusion change: yes: from 'no excess' to 'reversal supported for AI followers'

what: Opposite-direction rules from residual US leaders
original version: treated as tests of the reversal hypothesis
new version: reported, but not used as evidence for the reversal
why: the recurring rules were sector rotation (e.g. JNJ down -> Mitsubishi UFJ up), not gap reversal

original version: flat 10 bps per unit of turnover (20 bps round trip) for all markets
new version: per-market round trips: Japan 10 bps, Taiwan 0.15% day-trade tax + 5 bps, Korea transaction tax by year + 5 bps
why: transaction taxes differ a lot between markets (requested in review)
did the conclusion change: yes: from 'roughly break-even overall' to 'positive after costs in Japan only'

original version: reversal measured from the open only
new version: also measured from the close of the first hourly bar (hourly data, 2023-2026)
why: gap and open-to-close share the opening price, so noise in the opening print creates a negative correlation by construction (requested in review)
did the conclusion change: partly: about 60% of the reversal happens in the first hour; after 2+ SPY moves a significant part remains

original version: planned: residual against the home index
new version: residual against the mean of the other same-market stocks in our data

original version: residual target only
new version: residual and raw targets side by side
